newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot propane soars in week on U.S. values.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot propane soars in week on U.S. values.

text.p: Canada spot propane prices soared this week in line with wild prices in the U.S. and very cold weather in much of the U.S. and Canada, players said Thursday.
"It's bitterly cold," one liquified petroleum gas trader in western Canada said, noting temperatures well below freezing.
Forecasters are also calling for below to much below normal temperatures over the next 10 days throughout most of the U.S., driving up prices especially in the midcontinent.
In the western Canada hub of Edmonton, spot propane prices traded at 70.75 cents, an astonishing 20.00 cents above last Thursday levels. Contract prices are up to about 62.00 cents.

In the Sarnia hub in eastern Canada, spot material is up about 13.00 cents to between 65.60 cents and 66.50 cents a gallon. Players, however, said there is very little spot material available for trade.
Sarnia normal butane also jumped about 2.00 cents to 55.00/56.25 cents, on the strength of the U.S. and demand.
